newsitem.title: GERMANY: Beiersdorf five-month sales rise 6.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Beiersdorf five-month sales rise 6.6 pct.

text.p: German health-care products maker Beiersdorf said on Monday its group sales in the first five months of 1997 rose 6.6 percent, boosted mainly by exports.
Chairman Rolf Kunisch told the company's annual general meeting sales outside Germany were up 11.3 percent, while domestic sales rose only 1.5 percent.
He gave no forecasts for full-year sales or profits for the company, known for its Nivea-brand skin-care products. Hospital goods and Tesa-brand bandages remain the main sources of growth, he said.
In 1996, Beiersdorf showed a net profit of 233.8 million marks ($134.4 million) on sales of 5.78 billion marks.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.739 German Marks)
